parsed.why: Decriminalised and court-ordered gender-recognition rulings, but no administrative route, no current trans-specific violence data, and an unimplemented registration precedent. Exposure is mainly resident-facing; the lesbian-conduct provision stays unresolved and tangential.

Sexual-conduct ban repealed, Pride thriving, no recorded assaults on trans prisoners. Offsetting negatives are no gender-identity protection at work, friction over gender-neutral toilets, and a media-code residue. No documented border or facility exposure.

Retained life-imprisonment sodomy provisions, police extortion of LGBT people, and a magistrate barring a trans woman from court for her dress, with no hate-crime law. The 69-case violence count has no denominator, so it is only a pattern signal. Attitudes are improving.

No criminal ban, but documented violence, harassment and torture by police, security forces and army against LGBTQ people, plus militia violence with near-total impunity. No legal gender recognition, and expression is censored with imprisonment exposure.

Federal gender-identity protection and hate-crime coverage, self-declared marker change in some provinces, and an X marker. Negatives are identity-based prison placement with reported abuse, and school consent and healthcare rollbacks. Hate-crime rises and the LGBTQ-wide survey figure are weak trans-specific evidence.
